submitter: bugfix_168_deployed_asset_path (retraction lane, extending sweep coverage per handoff 2026-08-08b §3.3)
rationale:
The daily review-queue sweep (revalidate_review_queue) now covers five item_types. claims_unverified is not one of them, and nothing else closes it either: `SELECT status, count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='claims_unverified' AND status IN ('complete','verified')` returns ZERO ROWS on live clients_db (2026-08-09), and no row of the type carries a `deploy_result` payload, which is the tell that a real fix pipeline owns a type. Its producers set HandlerAgent "" by design, so there is no dispatch path, no handler, and no revalidator — 23 items across 7 sites, every one still `needs_human_review`. They are parked for ever by construction.

This is the same adoption this lane made for voice_tells on 2026-08-08 (council APPROVED r1, correlation 4d430ca8-7e34-479a-95f3-71fdc12fdef6), and it is being made the same way: run the CLOSER census FIRST (this lane once shipped a duplicate closer whose central claim was false and which 14 council seats accepted), share the emit-side scanner rather than restating its predicate, and make the scan report how much it actually read so that 'read nothing' cannot be mistaken for 'the copy is clean'.

ROUND 1 CORRECTION, and it was my error, caught by the editquality seat's gating objection. Round 1 claimed TWO converging producers (check_unverified_claims.go and check_unverified_claims_stats.go) and invoked the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 §1 as the authority for shipping without an RFC. THERE IS ONE PRODUCER, so that ruling never applied. check_unverified_claims_stats.go registers no check, has no init(), and emits no WorkItemSpec — it is a helper whose scanStoredStatClaims() is called from inside ScanDeployedClaims (check_unverified_claims.go:385 pages, :427 chrome) and nowhere else in production. Its header line 'reuses the existing claims_unverified item type' means it contributes findings to that type, not that it files items. The seat's sharper question — is the SCAN LOGIC shared, not merely the item_key shape? — is answered by that same call graph: there is ONE scan and both halves live inside it, so the revalidator cannot judge by a second producer's predicate because there is no second predicate. The change is SIMPLER than round 1 described it and no longer leans on a ruling that does not cover it. Separately, (2) The scan has NO page-status filter, unlike ScanVoiceTells which restricts to p.status IN ('active','deployed'). That difference is preserved deliberately: the revalidator must judge by exactly the predicate the emit side uses, or the two ends of an item's life answer the same question differently — which is the defect this sharing exists to prevent.

Evidence that this judges real change rather than running inert: 16 of the 23 pages have a page_components.updated_at later than the work item's created_at. A 0 there would have killed the change; it was the disconfirming check and it was run before the code was written.

plan.summary: Register a claims_unverified revalidator in the review-queue sweep. Extract the emit-side claims scan into a shared, exported ScanDeployedClaims so the revalidator re-runs the identical predicate instead of a second copy of it, and have that scan report how many components it actually examined so 'read nothing' cannot be mistaken for 'the copy is clean'. Move the locked-component skip out of SQL into Go so pinned components can be COUNTED rather than silently dropped. The verdict ladder is a pure function with every arm unit-tested, and `resolved` is reachable only from 'components were read and were clean'.

edits.rationale: Extract the page/site query plus the claim scans out of UnverifiedClaimsCheck.Run into an exported ScanDeployedClaims shared by both ends, and export the evidence-base loader. ClaimsPageScan carries ComponentsExamined and ComponentsSkippedLocked because len(Findings)==0 otherwise collapses three different states into one: copy fixed, nothing read, and only-locked-components-read. THE LOCKED SKIP MOVES FROM SQL TO GO: the page query carried `AND pc.locked_at IS NULL`, which dropped pinned rows before anything could count them, so a page whose only claims sit in a locked component was indistinguishable from a page that was cleaned up. Emitted output is unchanged: Run filters to pages with findings, so the work items this check files are byte-identical. ClaimFinding is a type ALIAS for the existing unexported unverifiedClaimFinding — the revalidator must be able to name the type it iterates, and the unexported spelling has ~20 use sites including this package's tests, so aliasing avoids churn that buys nothing. EMIT SIDE REWIRED IN THE SAME EDIT (previously filed separately; merged for round 4 because the gate caps a plan at 8 edits and these two are one refactor on one file, not two changes): Run now calls the shared scan with an empty pageIDFilter and filters to pages that actually carry findings, which is the half that keeps the refactor behaviour-preserving — the work items this check emits are byte-identical to before.

The drain itself. DB glue is split from a pure verdict ladder so every arm is testable without a database. Ladder order is load-bearing: 'still carries claims' is answered BEFORE 'some components were locked', or a page that still asserts a banned claim would be reported as unreadable rather than as still holding. Safe direction throughout: a wrong still_holds costs a human glance, a wrong resolved closes a live finding about an unsupported factual claim, so every arm that cannot answer returns `unknown`, which is non-terminal. The missing-page_id arm is also where the grouped site-chrome item lands — its item_key is the literal `claims:site_components` and its spec carries `surface`, not `page_id`. The item_key prefix is deliberately never parsed for a page id.

One map entry is the whole wiring: coveredItemTypes() is derived from reviewRevalidators, so registering the revalidator widens what the sweep selects in the same edit, with nothing else to remember and no second list to drift.

ROUND 5 — THIS EDIT NOW NAMES TestUnverifiedClaimsNeverResolvesWhenOnlyTheRegisterMoved, answering editquality's round-4 MEDIUM. The seat was right: grounded_in cited that test as the thing pinning the owner's copy-changed gate, and no edit added it, so the plan claimed a control it never filed. It is added HERE rather than as a ninth edit because the gate caps a plan at 8 edits and refuses a ninth CLIENT-SIDE before any credits are spent (097_TRIGGER line 101, `length <= 8`) — and because it is the same file and the same `add` operation as the tests already listed, not a second change smuggled into one slot. Its four cases are the four ways the gate can be wrong: component edited BEFORE filing, edited at EXACTLY the filing instant, no timestamp on any examined component, and no filing date on the item. The fourth case FAILED on first run and exposed a real defect — the code disagreed with its own doc comment about the zero-date case — which was fixed in the code, not the test. Every ladder arm exercised without a database. Two assertions are properties rather than cases: nothing reaches `resolved` without having examined a component (so a future reorder that closes an item on the strength of reading nothing fails even if each individual case still passes), and a fully-read clean page MUST resolve (a revalidator that can only say still_holds is the armed-but-inert shape this lane keeps finding, and registering one only adds scan cost).

This test pins the covered set and fails on any change, telling the author to update it and say why. It fired, as designed. The `want` list gains claims_unverified with the closer census and the two-producer note recorded beside it.

ROUND 3 — this is the OWNER'S ANSWER to the compliance seat's HIGH gating objection, which was raised identically in rounds 1 and 2 and which round 2 stated must be resolved by confirmed owner sign-off BEFORE the revalidator is wired live. The owner signed off WITH A CONDITION, choosing this over three costed alternatives (ship as-is; downgrade instead of closing; abandon). `resolved` now requires positive evidence that the PAGE moved: an EXAMINED component whose page_components.updated_at is later than the item's created_at. A register edit alone can no longer retract a finding. This is deliberately a mechanical control rather than a documented caveat, per the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 §2 — a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share. The zero-filedAt case is a SEPARATE arm because x.After(time.Time{}) is true for any real timestamp: folding it into the comparison would make an item with no known filing date close on any component edit however old, the exact inverse of the gate. That defect was real and briefly present — the header comment already claimed the correct behaviour while the code did not, and the property test caught the difference.

Supplies the gate's evidence from the scan that is already reading these rows, so no second query and no second predicate. Tracked for EXAMINED components only: a locked component's timestamp records a change to content this scan deliberately did not read, which is not evidence about the copy the finding was raised against. parkedReviewItem gains CreatedAt for the other side of the comparison — one more column from a row loadParkedReviewItems already selects, and its SELECT and rows.Scan are now flagged in-comment as one contract.

ROUND 4 — FILED AS ITS OWN EDIT, answering editquality's round-3 gating objection. The seat was right that the plan described this change only inside another edit's rationale, and right about the consequence it inferred: without it, filedAt arrives as the zero value and the ladder's IsZero() branch sends every item to `unknown` for ever, so the owner-mandated gate could never reach `resolved`. The CODE has carried this wiring since commit 9a9fef332 and is demonstrably working in production (see grounded_in: 8 closures on 2026-08-10, each carrying a real item_filed_at in its evidence) — what was defective was the PLAN, and this edit repairs that. parkedReviewItem gains CreatedAt; loadParkedReviewItems' SELECT gains created_at and its rows.Scan gains the matching destination. The SELECT and the Scan are one contract and are now flagged as such in-comment, because a column added to one and not the other is a silent scan error at runtime.
